note: Versions are pinned here so a build never silently upgrades (handoff_app_ios.md round 1). 'verified' says how each fact was established; 'status' NOT_VERIFIED/NOT_INSTALLED means the fact is still open and must not be read as passing.

go.verified: the version ci.yml, windows.yml and android.yml use; dev machine runs go1.26.6 darwin/arm64

x_mobile.pinned_by: native/core/go.mod tool block (gomobile, gobind), the same pin Android uses; built into a private tools directory, never a global install
x_mobile.decision: Same commit as Android (apps/android/toolchain.lock.json x_mobile.decision): newer x/mobile would move the desktop Core onto newer golang.org/x modules.

ios_bind.verified: 2026-10-16: gomobile bind of native/core/mobile with Go 1.26.6 and Xcode 27.0 succeeds without extra flags in about 44 s. Slices: ios-arm64 (arm64 only, 27 MiB) and ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator (x86_64 + arm64, 53 MiB; iossimulator includes x86_64 by default). Headers export MobileStart/Call/Stop/NetworkChanged/SetForeground and the MobilePlatform protocol. The device binary contains the Mihomo revision and no '/sbin/route', 'networksetup' or 'asterlink_tuntest' strings; the same scan finds both macOS strings in a darwin asterlink-core build (negative control).

xcode.verified: 2026-10-16: xcodebuild -version and xcodebuild -showsdks on the dev machine

ci.note: the Xcode ci.yml already uses for the macOS job; build number to be recorded from the first ios.yml run, not guessed. The simulator suite there uses the newest iOS runtime the image ships (--runtime latest).

simulator_runtime.verified: 2026-10-16: xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS installed iOS 27.0 Simulator (24A434, arm64, 8.05 GB) after go clean -cache freed about 23 GiB

signing.detail: no Apple Developer Program team and no iPhone yet; simulator builds are unsigned and every device case is BLOCKED (handoff_app_ios.md P1, P2)
